entry.summary: Governed Logic is the upstream, bidirectional reasoning architecture in which truth governs logic, logic governs reasoning, and reasoning remains answerable to its ultimate ground.

entry.title: Canonical definitions

entry.title: Sufficient grounding
entry.summary: Sufficiency asks whether a proposed ground can bear the explanatory, ontological, rational, semantic, or normative load placed upon it.

entry.title: On the Nature of Ultimate Grounding
entry.summary: A genuine termination occurs only when the load carried by the reasoning chain is actually borne by a ground sufficient for that load and ultimate with respect to the chain.

entry.title: Governed Logic Reasoning Systems
entry.summary: Truth must govern logic. Logic must govern reasoning. Reasoning is answerable back through logic to truth and ultimately to ground. Intelligence is downstream.
